items.title: 67259_Big Chief Moore oral history interview
items.q: Hugues Panassie was handling the bookings along with Mezzrow and Hugues was in our corner, our style of jazz.

ctx.x: That's right. Then a month later you went into the studio again and recorded "Wrap your Troubles in Dreams," "Rose Room," "Swinging with Mezz," "St. Louis Blues," "Big Butter and Egg Man," and "I Ain't Got Nobody." Do you remember those dates?

Oh, yes, yes, because Hugues Panassie was handling the bookings along with Mezzrow and Hugues was in our corner, our style of jazz. Incidentally, when Hugues wrote his "Guide to Jazz," or what was it, jazz critic book, I was included in it, he gave me a nice plug in his book. I was a guest at in his house, Fountainbleu."
Fountainbleau, that's where he resided for a number of years.
